$comment: Shared input/expected vectors for VfBreadcrumbs. The TypeScript rules in breadcrumbs/state.ts and the PHP mirror in packages/razor/src/Support/BreadcrumbsState.php both run this file. Three rules about items: which are current, whether one is a link, and the classes of one that is not. The rel derivation is not restated here because it is VfLink's rule, link/state-vectors.json, and both adapters call it. There is deliberately no vector for the router branch and none whose destination is an object: an object `to` is the Vue adapter's handoff to a component the reference never ships, pinned by the Vue characterization suite, and a vector for it would be the shared core describing a navigation contract that has no second implementation.

resolveBreadcrumbCurrentFlags.$why: One item with no flag is the last item, so it is current.
No flags: the last item is current and no other.
An explicit flag in the middle makes that item current; the last item is not.
Two explicit flags make two current items. The reference never enforces one.
An explicit false is the same as no flag: with no true flag, the last item is current.
An explicit flag on the last item is the same as the fallback.

isBreadcrumbLink.$why: A destination, not disabled, not current: a link.
The current item is never a link, even with a destination. Its href is dropped.
A disabled item is never a link, even with a destination.
An empty-string destination is no destination. This is where the component differs from VfLink, which keeps href="" on its anchor.
An explicit disabled=false is not disabled.
A string the reference would test as truthy - '0' is truthy in the reference's language, and the mirror must not read it as false.

resolveBreadcrumbItemClasses.$why: A non-link item that is not disabled: the block element only. The name is the reference's even when the item is not current.
Disabled adds the modifier after the block element.
